prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1426; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a third-party vehicle that entered on a late yellow. Police report requested. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness and has been seen at an urgent care facility. Claimant is represented by counsel; all contact to go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Received letter of representation from claimant's attorney's office. Requested medical authorization and prior treatment records for the neck and upper back. Recorded liability position as disputed pending review of the signal timing and witness statements. Scene photos from the insured's dashcam reviewed and added to file.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report. Officer noted both drivers gave conflicting accounts of signal phase. Independent witness contact information listed; recorded statement requested. Vehicle damage appraisal scheduled at repair shop. Diagnosis from treating physician indicates whiplash-type cervical strain with muscle spasm. Follow-up imaging ordered by provider.

Entry 4: Witness interviewed by phone and confirmed the third-party vehicle entered the intersection after the signal changed to red. Liability assessment revised to favor insured at a majority share. Demand package expected from claimant's counsel. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect current medical treatment and property damage estimates.

Entry 5: Counsel's demand package received, including itemized medical bills and treatment notes. Medical records under review by claims nurse for consistency with the reported mechanism of injury. Requested IME scheduling through counsel. File referred to supervisor for settlement authority review. Next diary set for follow-up with defense counsel on medical evaluation results.
